programme.desc: beIN STORY is a documentary event, lasting 70 to 90 minutes, looking back on a key moment in the history of sport or on a stadium legend. The program is presented by the journalist and one of the sport consultants concerned. Unforeseen event, athlete with a tragic destiny or crucial moment which changed a sporting discipline forever, beIN STORY presents major documentaries, some of which will be original creations from the beIN SPORTS editorial team, all with the analysis of the channel's specialists

programme.title: 30 for 30: Celtics/Lakers: Part 2
programme.desc: 30 for 30 (Sports). As part of its 30th anniversary celebration, ESPN looks back at notable sports happenings that occurred from 1979 to 2009 with this documentary series featuring 30 films from some of Hollywood's finest directors and producers. Peter Berg, Barry Levinson, John Singleton, Spike Jonze, Dan Klores, Barbara Kopple, Ron Shelton and Albert Maysles are among the filmmakers involved, and the stories told include the shocking trade of Wayne Gretzky in 1988, the Baltimore Colts' nighttime move in 1984, Reggie Miller's rivalry with the New York Knicks, the death of Len Bias in 1986, a profile of George Steinbrenner and his family business, and a look at Michael Jordan's attempt at a baseball career. A new series of 30 films premiered in October 2012 with «Broke,» about the challenges athletes face in managing their money

programme.title: Kieling's Wild World
programme.desc: Researchers are certain: We are currently experiencing the worst species extinction since the end of the dinosaurs. Animal filmmaker Andreas Kieling explores threatened habitats on three continents and speaks to researchers and animal rights activists. \n\nThe island of Madagascar, where Kieling observes ring-tailed lemurs, is almost a continent in itself. The jungle home of this lemur species is threatened by deforestation. In Alaska's Denali National Park, climate change is causing problems for many species - including the last 49 wolves that live and hunt there.

programme.title: Africa from above
programme.desc: Ethiopia is shaped by the forces of nature. While a lava lake bubbles in the crater of the Erta Ale volcano, salt workers transport the white gold of the Afar Depression through the surrounding desert. (Station info).

programme.title: Africa from above
programme.desc: Uganda is a place of spectacular contrasts: there are tropical rainforests and glacier-covered mountains. The country also has one of the fastest growing large cities. (Station info).

programme.title: Africa from above
programme.desc: The melancholic expanses of the Sahara and the largest solar park in the world: Morocco enchants with endless natural landscapes, cultural wealth and high-tech. (Station info).

programme.title: Africa from above
programme.desc: The landlocked African country of Zambia is located in the south of the continent. This country is home to the legendary Victoria Falls - and the world's largest mammal migration takes place here. (Station info).

programme.title: Africa from above
programme.desc: African, Arabic and Portuguese traditions come together in Mozambique. There are also endless sandy beaches, the Zambezi River and a perfectly preserved coral reef. (Station info).

programme.title: Africa from above
programme.desc: Cameroon, the country at the crossroads of West and Central Africa, combines tradition with progress. Here you will find eccentric art forms and imaginative inventions. (Station info).

programme.title: Africa from above
programme.desc: The landlocked African state of Botswana impresses with its wilderness landscape and endless swamp labyrinths. The continent's largest diamond manufacturer is also located here. (Station info).

programme.title: Into the Blue – Indonesiens Unterwasserparadiese
programme.desc: Between the Pacific and the Indian Ocean: The poisonous, black-banded sea snake roams the coral reefs here. She only briefly comes to the surface to breathe. (Station info).

programme.title: Into the Blue – Indonesiens Unterwasserparadiese
programme.desc: In the Lembeh Strait, mud and lava form an unusual biotope. Microorganisms are hidden inside - including the decorator crab with its pungent smell. (Station info).

programme.title: The Tuamotu Islands: natural wonders in the South Seas
programme.desc: The 240 small islands of Rangiroa are home to manta rays, dolphins and sharks, among others. The largest atoll in the Tuamotu archipelago is teeming with life. (Station info).

programme.title: Animals in the Eternal Ice

programme.title: Cheetahs: From cub to hunter

programme.title: Cats up close

programme.title: Game of Leopard Thrones – The Queen of the Leopards
programme.desc: Ruler Tingana is seriously ill and is fighting for survival. His territory and his family would be defenseless against a competitor. Is a rival taking advantage of the situation? (Station info).

programme.title: Forest of wild ponies
programme.desc: Great Britain's second-smallest national park in the south of the country has a lot to offer: The New Forest has served as a hunting ground since 1079 for King William the Conqueror (1027/28–1087). Since then, residents' livestock have been allowed to move freely in the forest and agriculture in the area has been stopped. Around 4,500 very special residents, the New Forest ponies, actively manage the landscape here alongside cattle, donkeys, pigs and sheep. The historic forest is therefore seen as a model for how species-rich landscapes in the middle of Europe can be preserved in the future. Apart from the deciduous and mixed forest, meadows and heathland make up over half of the nature reserve.

programme.title: Spines, fur and feathers

Điều tra.Trình bày: Hugo ClémentSản xuất: Andréa Orvain (Pháp, 2025)
